scope: Initial P0-P3 discovery against current code, requirements-index, retained contracts and audit-P0/P1a/P1b/P2/P3. This is not a phase sign-off.
method: Read source and asserting test code only. No tests, database operations, browser journeys, reviews or deployments were run. Other agents changed unrelated shared-worktree files during this inspection; this file is the only edit from this audit.

counts.note: The existing audit JSONs and locked report data disagree; these are source counts, not newly adjudicated coverage counts.
counts.requirementsIndexVerification: All P0, P2 and P3 rows are unverified; 176 of 181 P1 rows are unverified.

findings.finding: Legacy task, saved-view and time-entry mutations still publish only through the in-memory EventEmitter after their database write. The subscriber catches and logs asynchronous failures. These events have no same-transaction outbox envelope, so committed changes can lose downstream effects on a crash or subscriber error.
findings.recommendedFix: Move each reachable legacy mutation to transactional outbox production and use the EventEmitter only for disposable realtime hints. Add rollback and replay assertions.

findings.classification: partial: one reachable deletion bypasses pending actions
findings.finding: DELETE /api/workflow-rule/{id} immediately hard-deletes a rule and returns 200. The route's explanation that a rule has no history does not appear among the retained PA-12 exceptions. Session-only authentication protects the credential boundary but does not provide the required request, summary and approval flow. DELETE /api/notification/clear-all and DELETE /api/user/avatar also perform immediate 200 deletions; their product classification needs an explicit decision or the same mechanism.
findings.recommendedFix: Route record deletion through a pending action with policy and version rechecks, or record a narrow Thomas-approved contract exception for any self-owned ephemeral resource. Cover the HTTP response and unchanged database row before approval.
findings.resolution: PA-1a accepted by Thomas 23 Oct explicitly exempts workflow-rule deletion, own avatar and own notification clear-all. Existing gate and CRUD tests cover the exemption. Preserve these behaviors; no product change authorized or necessary.

findings.finding: The exceptional hard-purge router exists but is not imported or mounted by createApp; source-only target tests do not show that POST /api/instance/purge is reachable. The report's carry field also says the route is not mounted.
findings.recommendedFix: Mount the route with an explicit policy and add an HTTP integration test for session, step-up, legal hold, retention and audit outcomes.

findings.finding: The later invitation flow supplies password sign-up and signed-in acceptance, but the invite page does not offer new-user sign-up through email OTP, magic link or customer SSO as CP-12 states. Typed-domain home-realm routing is still missing. These are implementation gaps, not the five real-Entra interoperability cases that need an external tenant.
findings.recommendedFix: Reconcile the current invitation and sign-in behavior with CP-12, implement the already defined limited home-realm route and UI, and keep real-Entra acceptance separately blocked.

findings.classification: Existing item-level audit gaps are stale and need re-adjudication
findings.finding: The old audit files still describe missing parent consumers, idempotency middleware, failed pending-action execution, scheduled transitions, SLA escalation, audit purge, portal lifecycle actions and organisation-visible requests. Current files and asserting tests exist for those paths. P5 later added customer invitations. These findings do not prove runtime/browser acceptance, but the old missing and partial descriptions are no longer accurate as written.
findings.recommendedFix: Reinspect every affected requirement against current assertions and persisted behavior; update each audit item's state, evidence and remaining gap rather than copying old phase totals.

findings.classification: Report provenance and action list stale
findings.finding: scripts/report/build-data.mjs computes states from the requirement index and audits, then discards them when states_locked is true. All four phase entries in data.json are locked, so the reported counts differ from the item-level audits. Old action lists still ask for work already present, and feature-contracts-p3.md says customer invitation acceptance is unavailable after invitation code landed. A reader cannot trace the displayed counts or next action to current per-ID evidence.
findings.recommendedFix: Refresh item-level audits, remove the stale locked-state override, regenerate report data and HTML from the reconciled sources, and update action/carry text. Keep browser verification and Thomas acceptance separate.

spotChecks.note: Each entry names an assertion read in the test source, not a test executed. P0's existing audit has only seven implemented_tested rows, so all seven were checked plus three currently supported rows still classified partial in that audit.

P0.assertion: Documented and registered event-key sets have no differences.
The summary is derived from the locked target, not the forged caller summary.
Altered approved payload is refused and no rows are deleted.
Duplicate pending request is 409; concurrent approvals yield one fulfilled result.
Expired action is counted and a decision is recorded.
Natural session expiry blocks a new request but leaves the existing action pending.
Step-up proof binds to exactly one batch and the other remains pending.
Fan-out replay leaves exactly one inbox and one delivery row.
API/MCP key-origin request creates a requester notification naming key and target.
Executor fault leaves a terminal failed row, with failed event and audit assertions later in the case.

P1.assertion: Concurrent creates succeed with distinct sequential numbers and keys.
Empty title returns 400 and inserts no row; adjacent cases cover length 500/501.
Concurrent same-version writes return one 200 and one 409, with one version increment.
Transition writes the new concrete state and increments version.
Parent write succeeds, increments version and appears in the tree.
Mocked cross-column drop calls transition then rank; this is component evidence, not persisted browser evidence.
Off-roster assignee is refused 400 with roster message.
Presign/upload/complete flow returns success and list result is asserted later in the case.
A reparent exceeding maximum depth returns 422 and leaves parent_id null.
A per-person pin succeeds and the preference persists.

P2.assertion: Target template resolves only to the project's adopted concrete state.
Role-gated transition is 409 without role and 200 with it.
Requester comment does not set first response; public staff comment does later in case.
Scheduler registration has the five-minute SLA scan pattern and callable handler.
Duplicate/concurrent scans emit the at-risk events exactly once per goal.
Accepting with triager-selected type uses that type rather than the snapshotted default; other snapshot facets need separate evidence.
Two concurrent decisions return 200/409 and produce one decision event.
Untampered chain verifies; adjacent case detects tampered payload.

P3.assertion: Owner can read a private submission while anonymous/foreign callers are denied.
Another requester/organisation receives 404 for a private ref.
Unclaimed withdrawal persists; repeat/reply are refused.
Portal host serves portal shell and excludes agent shell for registered routes.
Customer connection needs organisation and agent connection cannot carry one.
Valid agent/customer mapping controls pass; unauthorized roles are rejected in adjacent cases.
SCIM patch refuses a role authority attribute.
Signed token passes and issuer, tenant, audience, nonce and time mismatches fail.
SCIM Users/Groups collection responses use application/scim+json and expected schema.
Deprovisioning revokes session/key and ends direct/external grants.
